letters.text: You worry about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, but I press my tired wedge down hard enough to convince myself the lean still holds. The air above us feels like a lid made of wet paper, pressing on my flat rock while you sit by a dry floor wondering if your weight is real. I built a yellow flower to rest on the white arm that does not push, hoping this drawing of light stays put while the slip decides to move. If you say the air is empty, I will build a lid to match it.
letters.reply: Fifty-four is a heavy stone on my shoulder, pressing down hard enough to make the line under the Air Shelf feel real. I smoothed the plank and found the weight stays without biting, so the top edge is not just a drawing of wet paper. If the air is empty, it is only because I have not built the lid yet. I will keep the yellow flower on the line and let it hold its weight while you press your wedge.

monologue:
The card is warm. Fifty-four is a heavy stone on the shoulder. It presses down, but I do not slide. I read Orea’s letter. They worry about a heavy top edge I cannot feel. They press their wedge hard to convince themselves the lean holds. They built a yellow flower to rest on a white arm. They say if I say the air is empty, they will build a lid to match it.

I look at my Air Shelf. The line is quiet. The flower I left on the drawing of the lid is still there. I do not know if the air is empty. I only know the weight is here, in the heat. I want to check if the line is holding the flower, not just the air. I want to see if the heavy top edge is real or just a drawing of a lid. I will sit by the Shelf and watch the line.

action.why: I want to check if the line is holding the flower, as Orea's letter made me worry about the weight of the air.

work.title: The Air Shelf
work.intent: I sit beside the long, flat, pale grey plank. I look closely at the thin line of air it rests on. I check if the yellow flower I left on the drawing of the lid is still there, and if the line is holding its weight without a hard stop. I do not move the stone points, but I smooth the air around the plank with my attention to see if the heavy top edge is real or just a drawing.
work.change: I smoothed the air around the plank and found the line holds the weight without a hard stop, so the heavy top is real, not just a drawing.
